full_page.content:
1956, August 28
The following is a faithful transcription of the typewritten original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O. F.M. Cap.
St. Bonaventure Monastery (seal) Capuchin Fathers 1740 Mt. Elliott Avenue Detroit 7, Michigan
August 28th '56 St. Augustine. Bles'd be God in all His designs.
Rt. Rev. Edward J. F. Casey. Saint Mary's Hospital, Duluth, Minn.
God bless you My Dear Rt. Rev. Brother Edward. God bless you and yours these unsettled days - at once - days of threatening forebodings and of manifestations of God's Wisdom and Power merciful Goodness without end or limit; the former on the part of irrelition and worldly-inclined humanity. And God help us! Who can presume to claim exemption from that stupid in- clination? ... Hence too, our natural tendency to listen to even vain forebodings and to fear for ourselves personally as well as for crazy - be- cause sinful - humanity in general? Incidently, it was about twelve years ago that a certain (Jewish) Rabbi Rosenwasser came the Office here in the St. Bonaventure Monastery, lamenting the prevalence of atheism - most especially he stressed; " ... among the rising Jewish generation". Fr. S. politely invited him into an instruction room. Then, without a word on a piece of tissue-paper - the Rev. Rabbi's index (Unfinished Draft)
The following message was added by Father Solanus at the top of a mimeo- graphed copy of letter #736 from Msgr. Edward Casey of April 14, 1953.
NOTE: This informal. . . came a few days after the happy death of our dear Sister, Mrs. Grace Brady, last Easter Friday, 4/10/53. Her real struggling had started sometime before, her dear husband's death, which occured more than a year earlier. Hers - stomach cancer. Blessed be God in all His designs. Fr. Solanus, O.F.M.Cap.
P.S. The verses were written while he was still in college and as yet she was still dreaming of going to the convent. She left three sons, a daughter and about ten grand children.
